audit_authority: Global OpenWrt Hardware Intelligence Team & OpenWrt Security Team

vulnerabilities.title: Dnsmasq DNS Cache Poisoning via Predictable TXID (DNSpooq)
vulnerabilities.description: A flaw in dnsmasq forward query logic allows remote attackers to spoof DNS replies and execute cache poisoning attacks due to insufficient entropy in query transaction IDs.
vulnerabilities.workaround: Enable DNSSEC verification or redirect local DNS queries through encrypted DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) upstream proxies.

vulnerabilities.title: Dnsmasq Heap Buffer Overflow in DNSSEC Validation Logic
vulnerabilities.description: Buffer overflow in the DNSSEC packet verification engine allows an attacker on the upstream WAN DNS reply path to trigger remote code execution or process crashes.
vulnerabilities.workaround: Upgrade to dnsmasq 2.83 or later, or disable DNSSEC validation temporarily if upgrading is impossible.

vulnerabilities.title: FragAttacks: Fragmentation Frame Injection as Plaintext Handshake
vulnerabilities.description: Vulnerability in IEEE 802.11 standards implementation in hostapd allowing an adjacent wireless attacker to inject unencrypted Wi-Fi frames that are accepted as legitimate handshake packets.
vulnerabilities.workaround: Enforce Protected Management Frames (PMF / 802.11w) on all wireless SSIDs.

vulnerabilities.title: U-Boot Ext4 Directory Traversal Memory Overwrite
vulnerabilities.description: Directory traversal vulnerability in the U-Boot ext4 filesystem parser allows local attackers with storage access to overwrite kernel memory during bootloader execution.
vulnerabilities.workaround: Use read-only SquashFS partitions and restrict physical access to USB storage ports during boot.

vulnerabilities.title: Linux Kernel mac80211 Use-After-Free in BSS Handling
vulnerabilities.description: A use-after-free in the mac80211 BSS management subsystem in the Linux kernel allows an adjacent wireless attacker to trigger a kernel panic or potentially execute arbitrary kernel-level code.

vulnerabilities.title: MediaTek mt76 Wireless Driver Buffer Overflow in Beacon Parsing
vulnerabilities.description: Buffer overflow flaw in the mt76 driver handling of malformed 802.11 beacon frames sent by a malicious wireless client or rogue access point.
vulnerabilities.workaround: Update OpenWrt to 22.03.2 or later containing updated kmod-mt76.

vulnerabilities.title: LuCI Web Interface Authenticated Command Injection
vulnerabilities.description: Improper input sanitization in certain LuCI RPC diagnosis endpoints allows authenticated administrators to execute arbitrary shell commands via unsanitized parameter passing.
vulnerabilities.workaround: Enforce strong administrator passwords, disable WAN LuCI access, and upgrade to OpenWrt 23.05.1+.

vulnerabilities.title: Terrapin Attack: SSH Channel Sequence Number Manipulation
vulnerabilities.description: Prefix truncation attack against SSH transport protocol when ChaCha20-Poly1305 or CBC cipher suites with Encrypt-then-MAC are negotiated, allowing an active Man-in-the-Middle attacker to drop initial extension negotiation messages.
vulnerabilities.workaround: Upgrade to OpenWrt 23.05.3+ containing strict key exchange extension (kex-strict).
